content.rendered:
Mumbai is where Indian pharma keeps its head office. The largest drugmaker in the country, Sun Pharma, is run from Goregaon, and Cipla, Lupin and Glenmark are all headquartered in the city, alongside the Indian arms of GSK and Novartis.

This guide profiles the pharmaceutical companies headquartered or based in Mumbai, from listed multinationals to small export and marketing firms. Every profile below was researched in November 2026 from company websites, registries and filings, and each company keeps the logo or photo it already had on this page.

Quick answer

If you only need the headline names, these are the Mumbai pharma companies most readers are looking for:

  • Sun Pharmaceutical Industries — India's largest pharma company, headquartered at Goregaon (East).
  • Cipla — founded in Mumbai in 1935, known worldwide for affordable generics and inhalers.
  • Lupin — Santacruz (East) headquarters, strong in generics, biosimilars and APIs.
  • Glenmark — Mumbai-based, focused on respiratory, dermatology and oncology.
  • GSK India and Novartis India — the listed Indian arms of two global groups, both run from Mumbai.
  • FDC and Aristo — long-established Mumbai formulation makers, incorporated in 1940 and 1971.

Pharma in Mumbai: a head-office capital

Mumbai's role in Indian pharma is concentrated at the top of the company rather than on the factory floor. The pattern repeats across this list: the boardrooms, regulatory teams and export desks sit in Mumbai, while large-scale manufacturing has mostly moved to dedicated industrial states.

  • Head offices: Sun Pharma (Goregaon), Cipla, Lupin (Santacruz East), Glenmark and FDC (Andheri) are all headquartered in the city, as are GSK India at Worli and Novartis India at Bandra Kurla Complex.
  • Manufacturing belt: the Thane–Belapur corridor in Navi Mumbai grew up as the city's production zone, and firms such as FDC still run plants across Maharashtra, but its listed plants also sit in Goa and Himachal Pradesh, which is typical of the industry today.
  • Finance and listings: most of the large names here are listed on the BSE and NSE, both headquartered in Mumbai, so investor relations and compliance teams are local too.
  • Trade and exports: the city's port and air-cargo links support export-led firms such as Infugen Pharma, which ships formulations from Mumbai to markets in Africa, South East Asia and beyond.
  • Smaller firms: below the listed majors sits a layer of marketing-led and niche companies, including a women's-health specialist (Cibeles), a dermatology marketer (AMET Healthcare) and a B2B sourcing platform (PharmaCompass).

Quick comparison — pharma companies in this guide

The table mixes very different kinds of business, from listed manufacturers to a sourcing platform and a German drug-delivery specialist. The profiles below explain what each one actually does, so read the detail before comparing them.

Detailed profiles

1. AMET Healthcare Private Limited

AMET Healthcare is an Indian healthcare company built around sales, marketing and distribution rather than its own factories. Its own website says it was established in 2013 and markets pharmaceuticals, wellness and other healthcare products in India and overseas.

Its stated specialism is dermatology and cosmetology: skin and hair care brands are its competitive focus, and it distributes partner brands across the rest of Maharashtra and Goa. That makes it a marketing partner for skincare brands rather than a contract manufacturer.

  • Established: 2013 (company website)
  • Focus: dermatology and cosmetology products
  • Business model: sales, marketing and distribution of healthcare products
  • Type: private limited company

2. Amnour Pharmaceuticals Pvt Ltd

Amnour Pharmaceuticals is a young, marketing-led formulations company. Its own website dates its establishment to 10 February 2021 and gives its office address at Pimpri, on the Old Mumbai–Pune Highway, so it serves the Mumbai market from the Pune side of the corridor.

Its brands appear on pharmacy listings across everyday categories: Calnoria calcium tablets, Esnoria-L for reflux and the Mucinour respiratory range are all marketed by Amnour, according to Apollo Pharmacy and 1mg product pages. The company says its products are manufactured for it at WHO-GMP and ISO certified plants.

  • Established: 10 February 2021 (company website)
  • Base: Pimpri, Pune, on the Old Mumbai–Pune Highway
  • Known brands: Calnoria, Esnoria-L and Mucinour (pharmacy listings)
  • Model: own brands made at certified partner plants (company statement)

3. Aristo Pharmaceuticals Private Limited

Aristo Pharmaceuticals is one of Mumbai's long-established private formulation makers. Ministry of Corporate Affairs records show it was incorporated on 8 November 1971 and registered in Mumbai, and it has traded for more than five decades since.

Its registered office is at Shah Industrial Estate, off Veera Desai Road in Andheri (West). The company remains privately held and focuses on branded formulations for the Indian market, sold through its own field force.

  • Incorporated: 8 November 1971 (MCA records)
  • Registered office: Andheri (West), Mumbai
  • Type: private limited company
  • Business: branded pharmaceutical formulations

4. Cibeles Pharmaceutical Private Limited

Cibeles is a nutritional and pharmaceutical company dedicated solely to women's healthcare, which makes it the niche specialist on this list. Company profile data records that it was registered in May 2019 and began market operations in March 2020.

It was formed in alliance with BDR Pharmaceuticals, which backs it with manufacturing and research support. Its registered office is in the Mahalaxmi area of Mumbai, and its credo, published on its own website, puts Indian women's health at the centre of the business.

  • Registered: May 2019; market operations from March 2020
  • Registered office: Mahalaxmi, Mumbai (MCA records)
  • Focus: women's healthcare and nutrition
  • Backing: formed in alliance with BDR Pharmaceuticals

5. Cipla Limited

Cipla is Mumbai's oldest big pharma name. It was founded in 1935 by Dr Khwaja Abdul Hamied as The Chemical, Industrial & Pharmaceutical Laboratories, and shortened its name to Cipla in 1984. The company is headquartered in Mumbai and listed on the Indian stock exchanges.

Cipla built its reputation on affordable medicines: it is a leader in respiratory products such as inhalers, and in 2001 it drew global attention by offering HIV antiretroviral treatment at a small fraction of the prevailing price. Its range today covers respiratory, cardiovascular, diabetes and anti-infective medicines.

  • Founded: 1935, by Khwaja Abdul Hamied
  • Headquarters: Mumbai
  • Type: public listed company
  • Known for: respiratory medicines, inhalers and affordable generics

6. F D C Limited

FDC began in 1936 as a partnership firm started by Anand Chandavarkar to import pharmaceutical dosage forms, infant foods and surgical goods. It was incorporated in 1940 as Fairdeal Corporation (Private) Limited, renamed FDC Private Limited in 1986, and listed on the BSE and NSE in 1996.

The company is best known as a pioneer of oral rehydration salts in India: its Electral brand is a household name, and it is also a significant maker of ophthalmic products. Its plants are at Roha, Waluj and Sinnar in Maharashtra, Verna in Goa and Baddi in Himachal Pradesh, while the head office stays in Mumbai.

  • Founded: 1936; incorporated as Fairdeal Corporation in 1940
  • Listed: BSE and NSE, 1996
  • Headquarters: Mumbai (Andheri West)
  • Known for: Electral oral rehydration salts and ophthalmics

7. GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Limited

GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Limited, known as GSK India, is the listed Indian subsidiary of the British biopharma group GSK plc. The Indian company was incorporated in 1924, originally as Glindia Limited, and took its present name in 2001 after the global Glaxo and SmithKline merger.

Its registered office is GSK House on Dr Annie Besant Road in Worli, Mumbai. GSK India manufactures, sells and distributes prescription medicines and vaccines across India, with a manufacturing facility at Nashik in Maharashtra supporting the business.

  • Incorporated: 1924 (as Glindia Limited)
  • Parent: GSK plc, United Kingdom
  • Registered office: GSK House, Worli, Mumbai
  • Focus: prescription medicines and vaccines

8. Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Ltd

Glenmark is a Mumbai-headquartered, listed pharmaceutical company founded in 1977 by Gracias Saldanha. It has grown from an Indian generics business into a company with branded and speciality products sold in markets around the world.

Its stated focus areas are respiratory, dermatology and oncology, and it combines a large generics portfolio with speciality brands. Glenmark's current logo, shown here, is taken from the company's own website.

  • Founded: 1977, by Gracias Saldanha
  • Headquarters: Mumbai
  • Type: public listed company
  • Focus: respiratory, dermatology and oncology

9. Infugen Pharma Pvt Ltd

Infugen Pharma is an export house for pharmaceutical formulations, run from Mulund (West) in Mumbai. Its website gives its head office at Runwal R Square on L B S Road, Mulund, and traces the business back to 1999.

The company specialises in oncology formulations alongside tablets, capsules, IV infusions and antibiotics, and says its oncology unit is WHO-GMP certified. It reports 115 products registered across 20 countries, with partners across Africa, South East Asia, Sri Lanka, Central America and the CIS.

  • Origins: 1999 (company website)
  • Head office: Mulund (West), Mumbai
  • Specialism: oncology and general formulation exports
  • Reach: 115 products registered in 20 countries (company statement)

10. Lupin Limited

Lupin was founded in Mumbai in 1968 by Dr Desh Bandhu Gupta, a chemistry professor who started the company to fight diseases of national priority, beginning with anti-tuberculosis medicines. It is now a listed, transnational company headquartered at Kalpataru Inspire, off the Western Express Highway in Santacruz (East).

Lupin sells branded and generic formulations, biotechnology products and active pharmaceutical ingredients in more than 100 markets. Its research base includes the Lupin Research Park near Pune, and the company is led today by the founder's family, including chief executive Vinita Gupta.

  • Founded: 1968, by Desh Bandhu Gupta
  • Headquarters: Santacruz (East), Mumbai
  • Type: public listed company
  • Known for: generics, complex generics, biosimilars and APIs in 100+ markets

11. Novartis India Limited

Novartis India Limited is the listed Indian arm of Novartis AG, the Swiss innovative-medicines group headquartered in Basel. Its registered office is at Inspire BKC in Bandra Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mumbai.

Unlike the generics-led companies on this list, Novartis India's business centres on patented, innovative medicines in speciality areas. The Mumbai office runs the Indian operations of the group, including medical, regulatory and commercial functions.

  • Parent: Novartis AG, Basel, Switzerland
  • Registered office: Inspire BKC, Bandra (East), Mumbai
  • Type: public listed company
  • Focus: innovative (patented) medicines

12. PharmaCompass

PharmaCompass is the odd one out on this list: not a manufacturer, but a digital B2B platform for the pharmaceutical industry. Registry data records the business, legally Lepro Pharma Compass OPC Private Limited, as founded in 2014.

The platform helps companies source active ingredients, finished formulations and excipients, and sells access to regulatory intelligence such as US drug master files (USDMFs), certificates of suitability (CEPs), prices, patents and inspection data. It is a research and sourcing tool used by procurement and business-development teams.

  • Founded: 2014 (registry data)
  • Legal name: Lepro Pharma Compass OPC Private Limited
  • Type: B2B marketplace and data platform
  • Covers: APIs, finished formulations, excipients, DMF and CEP data

13. RENAISSANCE PHARMACEUTICALS

Renaissance Pharmaceuticals is a Mumbai pharmaceutical company based at Andheri Industrial Estate on Veera Desai Road, Andheri (West). Its legal entity record (LEI) is active, and local business listings describe it as a pharmaceutical dealer and manufacturer operating since around 2006.

Public information about the company is limited beyond registry and trade data, which show it importing active ingredients and vitamins through Mumbai ports in recent years. Treat this profile as a starting point and verify licences and product range directly with the company before trading. (Limited public information.)

  • Base: Andheri Industrial Estate, Veera Desai Road, Andheri (West), Mumbai
  • Status: active registered entity (LEI record)
  • Activity: pharmaceutical manufacturing and trading
  • Note: limited public information; verify directly before trading

14. Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited

Sun Pharma is the biggest name on this list by a wide margin: India's largest pharmaceutical company and one of the world's largest specialty generics companies. It was founded in 1983 by Dilip Shanghvi, who remains its chairman and managing director.

Its headquarters is Sun House on the Western Express Highway at Goregaon (East), Mumbai. From there it runs a business spanning generics, branded formulations, consumer healthcare brands and active ingredients, and its 2014 acquisition of Ranbaxy consolidated its position at the top of Indian pharma.

  • Founded: 1983, by Dilip Shanghvi
  • Headquarters: Sun House, Goregaon (East), Mumbai
  • Type: public listed company
  • Known for: India's largest pharma company; specialty generics and chronic-care brands

15. LTS Lohmann Therapie-Systeme AG

LTS Lohmann is included because its logo appeared on this page and its technology is part of the Mumbai pharma story, but it is not a Mumbai company: it is a German drug-delivery specialist founded in 1984 and headquartered in Andernach, Germany. No Mumbai plant or office for LTS could be verified from public sources.

LTS develops and manufactures transdermal patches and oral thin films for pharmaceutical partners, with more than 20 marketed products built on its technology. If you are sourcing patch technology rather than a Mumbai supplier, LTS belongs on that separate shortlist.

  • Founded: 1984
  • Headquarters: Andernach, Germany
  • Specialism: transdermal patches (TTS) and oral thin films (OTF)
  • Note: technology partner, not a Mumbai-based company

How to choose a Mumbai pharma partner

The companies above do very different jobs, so match the type of business to what you actually need before comparing prices or terms:

  • For branded formulations and distribution muscle: look at the established Mumbai makers such as Aristo, FDC, Cipla, Lupin and Glenmark.
  • For exports and registrations in emerging markets: an export house such as Infugen Pharma is set up for exactly that work.
  • For a niche portfolio: Cibeles covers women's health, while AMET Healthcare offers dermatology-led marketing and distribution.
  • For sourcing and market data: use a platform such as PharmaCompass to find API and formulation suppliers and check their regulatory filings.
  • For drug-delivery technology: transdermal and oral-film specialists such as LTS Lohmann license technology rather than supplying the local market directly.

What to verify before you sign or order

  • Manufacturing and wholesale drug licences issued by the Maharashtra FDA, checked against the legal name on the licence.
  • Current company status and directors on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs registry, especially for smaller private firms.
  • GMP and WHO-GMP certificates for the actual plant that will make your product, not just the brand making the claim.
  • For listed companies, the latest annual report and exchange filings, which are public on BSE and NSE.
  • Product-level registrations and trademarks for any brand you plan to distribute, confirmed on the label and with the marketer named on it.

Frequently asked questions

Which is the largest pharma company headquartered in Mumbai?

Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, headquartered at Sun House, Goregaon (East). It is India's largest pharmaceutical company and one of the largest specialty generics companies in the world.

Which companies in this guide are listed on the stock exchanges?

Sun Pharma, Cipla, Lupin, Glenmark, FDC, GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals and Novartis India are all publicly listed in India. Aristo, AMET Healthcare, Cibeles, Infugen, Amnour and Renaissance are private companies, and PharmaCompass is a private digital platform.

Do these companies manufacture inside Mumbai?

Mostly, no. Mumbai hosts their head offices, and some production remains in the wider region, including the Thane–Belapur belt in Navi Mumbai. Large plants are usually in other states: FDC, for example, manufactures in Maharashtra, Goa and Himachal Pradesh.

Which Mumbai pharma company focuses on women's healthcare?

Cibeles Pharmaceutical Private Limited, registered in 2019 and backed by BDR Pharmaceuticals, works only in women's healthcare and nutrition.

Which company here is known for oral rehydration salts?

FDC Limited, the Mumbai company behind Electral. FDC began as Fairdeal Corporation in the 1930s and is regarded as a pioneer of ORS in India.

How can I check a small Mumbai pharma firm before trading with it?

Start with the checks in the verification section above: MCA status, Maharashtra FDA licences and plant-level GMP certificates. Where public information is thin, as with Renaissance Pharmaceuticals on this list, verify everything directly with the company.

This guide was researched and rewritten in November 2026 from company websites, corporate registries and stock-exchange information. Company details change, so confirm anything you plan to rely on with the company itself.

title.rendered: Top 62 Pharma Companies in Chandigarh Tri-city (2026)

content.rendered:
Chandigarh's pharmaceutical trade is not centred on factories inside the city. It is centred on offices. Most of the 62 companies in this guide sell, market or arrange manufacture from Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula, while the actual plants sit in the Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh belt of Himachal Pradesh or in nearby industrial estates such as Derabassi and Barwala.

This guide was researched afresh in November 2026: company websites first, then corporate registry records and established trade directories. Every profile states what could be verified, marks company claims as claims, and keeps each company's existing logo in place. Use the quick answer and the comparison table to shortlist, then verify licences before you sign anything.

Quick answer

  • Most of these 62 companies are PCD franchise and marketing businesses, not factory owners. Manufacturing usually happens at units in Baddi, Nalagarh, Derabassi or Barwala.
  • The oldest names by registry date are Ultra Chiron Pharmaceuticals (1993), Focus Healthcare (1998), Sanify Healthcare (2003) and Sanctus Global Formulations (2008, founded as Crescent Therapeutics).
  • The only national listed major with a tricity plant is Sun Pharma, whose SEZ unit operates at Phase VIII-A, Mohali.
  • Two entries, PharmaAdda and Pharmahopers.com, are online platforms rather than manufacturers. Their profiles say so plainly.
  • Before paying any franchise deposit, verify the company's drug licence, the manufacturing site's WHO-GMP certificate and the exact legal entity name on the agreement.

How the Chandigarh tricity pharma cluster works

A Department of Pharmaceuticals cluster survey counted 43 pharmaceutical units in the Panchkula cluster and 80 in the Derabassi cluster in SAS Nagar district. Across the state border, the same survey counted about 400 units in the Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh belt in Solan district. That belt grew after the central industrial package of June 2003 and sits roughly 45 minutes from Chandigarh by road.

Chandigarh itself plays a different role. Its Industrial Area Phase 1 and Phase 2, and the Motor Market at Manimajra, are dense with registered offices, marketing offices and franchise headquarters of companies whose products are made elsewhere. Panchkula adds the HSIIDC estates at Barwala and Alipur, and Mohali adds JLPL Sector 82, Derabassi and Zirakpur. One directory, PharmaAdda, counts about 800 pharma companies registered across Chandigarh and the tricity.

  • Where the factories are: the Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh belt (Solan, Himachal Pradesh) is the main formulation zone. CDSCO runs a zonal office at Baddi covering Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.
  • Where the offices are: Manimajra Motor Market and Industrial Area Phase 1 and 2 in Chandigarh; HSIIDC Barwala and Alipur and Industrial Area Phase 1 and 2 in Panchkula; JLPL Sector 82, Derabassi and Zirakpur in Mohali district.
  • The dominant business model is PCD (propaganda-cum-distribution) franchising, where a local partner gets district-level monopoly rights to market a company's brands.
  • The second model is third-party or contract manufacturing, where brands outsource production to units in Baddi, Nalagarh or Derabassi and concentrate on sales.
  • Industry blogs often estimate that the BBN belt produces 35 to 45 per cent of India's formulations. Treat those figures as industry estimates, not official statistics.

Its ranges cover paediatrics, antibiotics, gastro and PPI lines, cardiac-diabetic care, gynaecology and dental products. It states that its plant works to WHO-GMP and ISO standards. Its division Bluewater Research appears earlier in this list.

  • Based in: Sector 25-D, Chandigarh; plant at Jharmajri, Baddi
  • Since: 2010
  • Model: third-party manufacturing
  • Forms: tablets, capsules, syrups, softgels, powders, ointments, nutraceuticals
  • Claims (company): WHO-GMP and ISO standards at the plant
  • Division: Bluewater Research

37. Logos Pharma

Logos Pharma is a contract and third-party manufacturing specialist. A company profile dates its first manufacturing facility to 1994, which makes it one of the longest-running manufacturers connected to this list. Its factory is at Village Maissa Tibba, Nalagarh, in Solan district, and its office is at Industrial Area Phase 1, Chandigarh.

The plant makes tablets and hard gelatin capsules, including dedicated beta-lactam and cephalosporin blocks, across more than 100,000 square feet of built-up area, according to the director's message on the company website. Directors Ankur Gupta and Anuj Gupta lead the business. Profiles describe GMP, GLP and ISO 9001:2015 systems.

  • Based in: Industrial Area Phase 1, Chandigarh (office); Maissa Tibba, Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh (factory)
  • Since: first facility in 1994 (company profile)
  • Directors: Ankur Gupta and Anuj Gupta
  • Model: contract and third-party manufacturing
  • Speciality: tablets and hard gelatin capsules, with beta-lactam and cephalosporin blocks

38. Medbeat Healthcare

Medbeat Healthcare is a partnership firm established in 2019, according to Justdial's statutory listing, and works from Plot 295, Industrial Area Phase 2, Panchkula. Partner Parav Goyal leads the business. Medbeat runs a PCD franchise and arranges third-party and contract manufacturing, with production placed at facilities in Baddi, according to its website.

  • Based in: Panchkula
  • Since: 2019 (Justdial statutory details)
  • Leadership: Parav Goyal (partner)
  • Model: PCD franchise; third-party and contract manufacturing
  • Forms: tablets (beta-lactam and non-beta-lactam), capsules, dry syrups, oral liquids, external products, nutraceuticals
  • Claims (company website): ISO 9001:2015 certified; more than 350 product approvals for third-party work

39. Medons India

Medons India is a Panchkula-based PCD franchise company established in 2011. Directory sources describe it as the allopathic division of H & Care Incorp, and its website gives an address at Plot 344, Industrial Area Phase 2, Barwala, the same plot as H & Care's headquarters. Chief executive Munish Goyal leads the business.

Medons is best known for its dermatology and cosmetic range: creams, ointments, gels, lotions, serums, dusting powders, soaps and shampoos. It also runs a general allopathic range and lists antibiotics and anti-infectives, anti-cancer products, capsules and liquid ampoules and vials among its specialities. It offers franchise rights on a monopoly basis and states ISO 9001:2015 certification.

  • Based in: Panchkula (Plot 286, Industrial Area Phase 1 registered address; Barwala office)
  • Since: 2011
  • Leadership: Munish Goyal
  • Model: PCD franchise with monopoly rights; third-party manufacturing
  • Known for: dermatology and cosmetic formulations, plus a general allopathic range

40. MONARK Biocare Pvt Ltd

MONARK Biocare was incorporated on 18 November 2011 and is registered at Plot 250, HSIIDC, Alipur, Barwala, Panchkula, with a corporate address at Plot 201 in the same estate. The company offers contract manufacturing and a monopoly PCD franchise. It states ISO certification and WHO-GMP and GLP certified production, with DCGI-approved formulations.

  • Incorporated: 2011 (CIN U24232HR2011PTC044353)
  • Based in: Barwala, Panchkula
  • Model: contract manufacturing and monopoly PCD franchise
  • Forms: tablets, capsules, syrups, injectables, ointments
  • Segments: antibiotics, anti-infectives, pain management, cardiovascular
  • Associated brand: Norchem Healthcare (per Tracxn)

41. Morstella Biotech

Morstella Biotech is a division of Kryptomed Formulations, according to its own corporate brochure, and shares Kryptomed's Panchkula office at SCO 54, Sector 11. Chief executive Rajan Madan leads the division. Morstella works in sales and distribution of finished dosage formulations and offers a PCD franchise, claiming more than 150 products launched.

  • Parent: division of Kryptomed Formulations Pvt Ltd
  • Based in: Sector 11, Panchkula
  • Leadership: Rajan Madan
  • Model: sales and distribution; PCD franchise
  • Claims (company): ISO 9001:2015 certified; 150-plus products launched
  • Note: the group's directors also co-own a drug testing laboratory, Shagun Medi Testing, per the group brochure

42. NEOLINA Pharmaceuticals

NEOLINA Pharmaceuticals is a sole proprietorship of Sumit Papneja, working from SCF 50, Industrial Area Phase 1, Panchkula. The business dates to 2019. Its model is distinctive: one franchise partner per district, confirmed with a written monopoly letter. Its own website puts the range at more than 300 formulations across more than 17 therapy categories.

Neolina describes itself as a licensed drug distributor whose products are made by WHO-GMP certified manufacturing partners. It says it dispatches to more than 28 states. Its ranges cover antibiotics, pain management, gastro and liver care, vitamins and nutrition, respiratory, paediatrics, women's health, cardiac care and herbal products.

  • Based in: Panchkula
  • Since: 2019
  • Leadership: Sumit Papneja (proprietor)
  • Model: PCD franchise, one partner per district with a written monopoly letter
  • Forms: tablets, capsules, syrups, drops, sachets, injections, ointments, softgels, dry syrups

43. NOVALAB Health Care Pvt Ltd

NOVALAB Health Care works from Industrial Area Phase 1, Panchkula, under managing director Pankaj Kumar Agarwal. The company's website claims roughly two decades in the business and a group of specialist divisions, while IndiaMART records the present company as established in 2014. It offers a PCD franchise and puts its range at more than 1,000 products, a company figure.

  • Based in: Plot 208 (HSIIDC Industrial Shed 208), Industrial Area Phase 1, Panchkula
  • Leadership: Pankaj Kumar Agarwal (managing director)
  • Model: PCD franchise; trader and manufacturer of tablets, capsules, injections and syrups (IndiaMART)
  • Segments (company website): cardiac, diabetic, derma, gynae, paediatric and general
  • Claims (company): WHO-GMP and ISO 9001:2015 certification; about nine to ten associated divisions

44. Pasco Pharmaceutical

Pasco Pharmaceutical works from Plot 840, JLPL Industrial Area, Sector 82, Mohali, according to its own product list; an earlier Chandigarh address also appears in directories. It describes itself as an ethical pharma company running a franchise programme on a monopoly basis. Its product list carries ISO 9001:2015 certification.

  • Based in: Sector 82, Mohali
  • Model: ethical pharma marketing; PCD franchise on a monopoly basis
  • Forms: liquids, tablets, capsules and injections, plus soft-gel capsules, dry syrups and ointments
  • Claims (company): ISO 9001:2015 certified; WHO-GMP manufacturing site

45. Pharma Drugs & Chemicals

Pharma Drugs and Chemicals, which also uses the name Pharma Drugs and Chemicals Unlimited, is one of the oldest names here: its PharmaHopers profile dates the consolidated business to 1990. It is registered at Pabhat Road, Zirakpur, and led by chief executive and marketing director Arvind Kapila. It offers a PCD franchise and third-party manufacturing.

  • Based in: Pabhat Road, Zirakpur
  • Since: 1990 (company profile)
  • Leadership: Arvind Kapila
  • Model: PCD pharma franchise and third-party manufacturing
  • Range: pharmaceutical products, nutraceuticals and ayurvedic products
  • Segments: antibacterial, anti-diabetic, anti-hypertensives, anti-inflammatory, and liver and stone preparations
  • Forms: tablets, capsules, softgelatin, syrups, injectables, ointments and beta-lactams
  • Claims (profile): GMP and ISO 9001:2008 standards; 30 years of experience

46. Zencus Pharma

Zencus Pharma works from Plot 286, Industrial Area Phase 1, Panchkula, and describes itself as Chandigarh-based. Chief executive Kapil Jindal leads the company. A franchise listing dates its establishment to 2016 and its range at more than 500 products. Zencus offers a PCD franchise with district-wise monopoly rights, third-party manufacturing and bulk order supply.

  • Based in: Panchkula
  • Leadership: Kapil Jindal
  • Model: PCD franchise with district-wise monopoly; third-party manufacturing
  • Range: allopathic and ayurvedic medicines
  • Brands in its listings: Monozen (ceftriaxone injections), Rictocal K27, Proticus protein powder, Diczen-SP
  • Claim (company): WHO-GMP certified

47. PharmaAdda

PharmaAdda is not a manufacturer. It is an online directory and discovery platform for the pharmaceutical industry, publishing location-wise lists of companies in Chandigarh, Mohali and Derabassi, along with PCD franchise and manufacturer category lists, with company addresses and product details. The platform says its team verifies companies before listing them. It is kept in this guide because the original list carried it, and because buyers use it to find tricity suppliers.

  • Type: B2B directory and discovery platform (pharmaadda.in)
  • What it lists: company profiles for PCD franchise, third-party manufacturing and manufacturer searches
  • Sector figure it publishes: almost 800 pharma companies registered in Chandigarh including the tricity, citing a Smartscrapers count of 354 pharma companies in Chandigarh as of 15 October 2025

48. Pharmahopers.com (PharmaHopers)

Pharmahopers.com, usually written PharmaHopers, is a business-to-business online marketplace built only for the pharmaceutical industry. Its own company history dates its launch to December 2016. It is based at SCO 18, Sector 16, Panchkula. Manufacturers, traders, distributors, wholesalers, importers, exporters and service providers use it to publish company profiles and product catalogues.

Many of the factsheets used to research this guide come from PharmaHopers profiles, which is typical of its role in the tricity trade: it is the shop window through which many Panchkula and Chandigarh franchise companies are found. It is a platform business, not a medicine manufacturer.

  • Type: B2B pharma marketplace (pharmahopers.com)
  • Based in: SCO 18, Sector 16, Panchkula
  • Since: launched December 2016 (company history)
  • Role: company profiles and catalogues for manufacturers, traders, distributors, wholesalers, importers and exporters

49. Pritus Healthcare Pvt Ltd

Pritus Healthcare works from SCF 289, Motor Market, Manimajra, Chandigarh. It offers a PCD franchise with district-wise monopoly rights, third-party manufacturing and pharma distribution. Directory listings put its range at more than 300 products with a focus on chronic and general formulations, and one listing claims more than 500 existing franchises; treat that figure as marketing.

  • Based in: Manimajra, Chandigarh
  • Model: PCD franchise; third-party manufacturing; distribution
  • Forms: tablets, capsules, injectables, syrups, paediatric drops, oils, powders, ointments, sachets
  • Segments: antihistamines, ophthalmic, antimicrobials, gynaecology, antibiotics, paediatrics, gastrointestinal, orthopaedic, dermatology
  • Claims (listings): WHO-GMP and ISO compliant

50. Salvus Pharma

Salvus Pharma works from Plot 633, JLPL Industrial Park, Sector 82, SAS Nagar, Mohali. Managing director Raman Lamba leads the company. Salvus states ISO 9001:2015 certification on its website and offers a PCD franchise on a monopoly basis plus third-party manufacturing. Its website also lists an administrative office in Landau, Germany.

  • Based in: Sector 82, Mohali
  • Leadership: Raman Lamba (managing director)
  • Model: PCD franchise on a monopoly basis; third-party manufacturing
  • Forms: tablets, capsules, injections, syrups, softgels, protein powders, ointments, nutraceuticals, drops, sachets
  • Segments: cardiac-diabetic, antibiotics, gynaecology and a dedicated dental range
  • Claims (company and IndiaMART): 1,000-plus molecules; 500 existing franchises

51. Sanctus Global Formulations Ltd

Sanctus Global Formulations is the clearest example here of the Chandigarh incorporation and Baddi plant pattern. A CARE Ratings profile records that the company was incorporated in October 2008 at Chandigarh as Crescent Therapeutics Limited, that the business was taken over by the Joshi family in February 2017, and that it was renamed in April 2018.

Its plant stands at Village Kunjhal, behind Jharmajri, Barotiwala, Baddi, and specialises in oral solid dosage forms: tablets and capsules, plus direct compression granules, pellets, powders and nutraceuticals. The company describes the plant as WHO-GMP certified and offers contract manufacturing and a PCD franchise. Product labels confirm real output: medicines sold by other brands list Sanctus as their manufacturer.

  • Incorporated: October 2008 at Chandigarh, as Crescent Therapeutics Limited (CARE Ratings)
  • Plant: Khasra 587/588, Village Kunjhal, Barotiwala, Baddi, Himachal Pradesh
  • Model: contract and third-party manufacturing; PCD franchise
  • Speciality: oral solid dosage forms, tablets and capsules

52. Sanify Healthcare Pvt Ltd

Sanify Healthcare was incorporated on 14 October 2003, which gives it more than two decades in the tricity trade. Its registered office is at Dhakoli, Zirakpur, and it operates from Plot 1323, JLPL Industrial Area, Sector 82, Mohali. Registry data classifies the company as a manufacturer of allopathic pharmaceutical preparations, with trade forming the majority of its turnover.

Sanify runs an ethical PCD franchise across India with district-level monopoly rights. Its website puts the range at more than 500 DCGI-approved products across antibiotics, paediatrics, gynaecology, cardiac care, dermatology, diabetic care and ENT. The company states that its manufacturing facilities are WHO, GMP and ISO certified.

  • Incorporated: 14 October 2003 (CIN U24232PB2003PTC026452)
  • Based in: Plot 1323, JLPL Industrial Area, Sector 82, Mohali; registered office at Dhakoli, Zirakpur
  • Model: ethical PCD franchise with monopoly rights
  • Forms: tablets, capsules, syrups and injectables (company website)

53. Sepik Life Sciences

Sepik Life Sciences works from Plot 14, Industrial Area Phase 2, Panchkula. It is a PCD franchise company that describes a presence across Chandigarh, Panchkula and Mohali. Its own website claims more than 25 years of experience and carries a large live catalogue: more than 200 tablet products alone, plus syrups and paediatric lines, injectables, gastro and PPI ranges, ayurvedic products and softgels.

  • Based in: Panchkula
  • Model: PCD pharma franchise
  • Catalogue (own website): tablets, syrups and suspensions, injectables, gastro and PPI range, ayurvedic products, softgels
  • Example brand on its website: Citisep syrup (citicoline and piracetam)
  • Claim (company): over 25 years of experience

54. ShinePro Life Sciences Pvt Ltd

ShinePro Life Sciences was incorporated on 16 February 2021 and works from Plot 331, Industrial Area Phase 1, Panchkula. Registry reporting describes it as a subsidiary of Mits Healthcare Private Limited, working in pharmaceutical wholesale and distribution. Its IndiaMART profile carries older text dating the business to 2010; the 2021 registry date is the reliable one.

  • Incorporated: 2021 (CIN U24230HR2021PTC092948)
  • Parent: subsidiary of Mits Healthcare Private Limited (per The Company Check)
  • Based in: Panchkula
  • Model: wholesale trading and distribution; PCD franchise
  • Mentor named in listings: M. K. Bhatia
  • Range traded: pharmaceutical tablets, capsules, oral solutions and critical-care injectables

55. SJK Pharmaceutical Pvt Ltd

SJK Pharmaceutical was incorporated on 30 July 2008 and works from Plot 79, Industrial Area Phase 9, Mohali. Director Rupinderjit leads the company. SJK manufactures and supplies formulations with a visible strength in liquid orals: its catalogues list long ranges of syrups and suspensions alongside tablets, capsules and ointments, and it offers third-party manufacturing and PCD franchise arrangements across India.

  • Incorporated: 2008 (CIN U24119PB2008PTC032156)
  • Based in: Mohali
  • Leadership: Rupinderjit (director)
  • Model: manufacturer, distributor and supplier; third-party manufacturing; PCD franchise
  • Known for: syrups and suspensions, plus listings for aceclofenac-paracetamol tablets, albendazole suspension and amikacin injection

56. Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd (Sun Pharma)

Sun Pharmaceutical Industries is the one national major in this list, and its tricity link is a factory, not an office. Sun Pharma operates a formulation plant at Plot A-41, Industrial Area Phase VIII-A, SAS Nagar, Mohali, listed in company location records as its SEZ Unit-I. Sun Pharma is India's largest pharmaceutical company and the world's fourth largest specialty generics company.

The Mohali plant came to Sun Pharma through its 2015 acquisition of Ranbaxy Laboratories, as Business Standard reported in March 2017 when the US FDA lifted the plant's import alert and removed its Official Action Indicated status, clearing it to supply approved products to the US market. Sun Pharma's head office is in Mumbai; the Mohali unit is its tricity manufacturing presence.

  • Tricity presence: SEZ Unit-I formulation plant, Plot A-41, Phase VIII-A, Mohali
  • Parent: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd, headquartered in Mumbai
  • How it arrived: inherited with the Ranbaxy Laboratories acquisition in 2015
  • Regulatory note: US FDA lifted the Mohali plant's import alert in 2017 (Business Standard)

57. Ultra Chiron Pharmaceuticals Pvt Ltd

Ultra Chiron Pharmaceuticals was incorporated on 20 July 1993, making it the oldest company in this list by registry date. Its registered office is at Plot 80, Industrial Area Phase II, Chandigarh. Managing director Sanjeev Singal has been associated with the company since incorporation, with Amrik Singh as whole-time director. Its PharmaHopers profile lists an operating address at Focal Point, Phase 9, Mohali, and describes it as a manufacturer of tablets, drops and creams that also offers a PCD franchise.

  • Incorporated: 1993 (CIN U24231CH1993PTC013535)
  • Based in: Chandigarh (registered office); Mohali operating address per its profile
  • Leadership: Sanjeev Singal (managing director); Amrik Singh (whole-time director)
  • Model: manufacturer and PCD franchise
  • Forms (profile): pharmaceutical tablets, drops and creams

58. United Laboratories

United Laboratories is a Derabassi-based manufacturer in the wider tricity orbit, founded in 2015 by Munish Goel, with Shubham Goel as chief executive, according to its website. Its units stand at Hansa Industrial Park on Barwala Road, Derabassi, and at Village Bhagwanpura, Derabassi. The company specialises in third-party manufacturing of nutraceutical and ayurvedic products.

Its range covers tablets, capsules, softgels, gummies, powders, syrups and effervescent products, plus skincare lines, with more than 200 products claimed on its website. The company says its units are ISO and WHO-GMP certified and FSSAI approved for nutraceuticals, and that it exports to markets including the USA, Europe, South Africa and parts of Asia.

  • Based in: Derabassi, Mohali district (two units)
  • Since: 2015 (company website)
  • Leadership: Munish Goel (founder); Shubham Goel (chief executive)
  • Model: third-party and contract manufacturing; private label
  • Focus: nutraceuticals, ayurvedic products, softgel capsules and effervescent tablets

59. Ve-Nutra Pharma

Ve-Nutra Pharma is a nutraceutical manufacturer at Plot 131, HSIIDC, Alipur, Barwala, Panchkula. Industry listings date the business to 2020 and describe ISO 9001:2015 certification. It works in third-party and contract manufacturing and private labelling, with a stated strength in soft gelatin capsules. Its supplements target women's health, energy, weight management and sports nutrition, and it also supports PCD franchise partners.

  • Based in: Barwala, Panchkula
  • Model: third-party nutraceutical manufacturing and private labelling
  • Segments: cardiology, dermatology, digestive supplements, gynaecology and neurology
  • Claim (company): products made under WHO-GMP certified units
  • Also offers: PCD pharma franchise with district-wise monopoly rights

60. Ventus Pharmaceuticals Pvt Ltd

Ventus Pharmaceuticals was incorporated on 14 November 2011, though the company's own profile traces the business back to 2009 in Chandigarh. It works from Plot 216, HSIIDC Industrial Estate, Alipur Barwala, Panchkula, with a corporate office at Swastik Vihar, MDC Sector 5, Panchkula. Managing director Girjesh Kumar Singh and director Shaishav Sandal lead the company.

Ventus is a PCD franchise marketing company. Its brochure puts the range at more than 350 molecules and over 500 DCGI-approved products; treat those as company figures. Ranges cover general medicines, gynaecology, orthopaedics, critical care, neuropsychiatry, ayurvedic and nutraceutical lines. Its division Caresal Pharma sells from the same Barwala base.

  • Incorporated: 2011 (business traced to 2009 by the company)
  • Based in: Barwala and MDC Sector 5, Panchkula
  • Leadership: Girjesh Kumar Singh (managing director); Shaishav Sandal (director)
  • Model: PCD pharma franchise marketing
  • Claim (company): ISO 9001:2015 certified

61. Vibdrugs Biosciences

Vibdrugs Biosciences is a proprietorship of Amit Rawat, started in 2014 at Chandigarh. It works from SCF 427, Motor Market, Manimajra, and also lists an address at Plot 274, Industrial Area Phase 1, Panchkula. Vibdrugs is a PCD franchise company offering district-wise monopoly rights. Its own presentation puts the range at more than 500 DCGI-approved formulations, a company figure.

  • Based in: Manimajra, Chandigarh; also Panchkula
  • Since: 2014
  • Leadership: Amit Rawat (proprietor)
  • Model: PCD pharma franchise with monopoly rights
  • Divisions (company): general, gynae, derma, paediatric, ortho, cardiac-diabetic
  • Forms: tablets, capsules, syrups, injectables, ayurvedic products, respules, creams, eye and ear drops

62. ZOYDEC Pharmaceuticals Pvt Ltd

ZOYDEC Pharmaceuticals is the youngest incorporated company in this list. It was incorporated on 31 December 2020 and is registered at SCF 283, Motor Market, Manimajra, Chandigarh. Registry records name directors Rohan and Pardeep Kumar Singh. ZOYDEC offers a PCD franchise on a monopoly basis across India and third-party manufacturing, with DCGI-approved formulations claimed in its profiles.

  • Incorporated: 2020 (CIN U24230CH2020PTC043424)
  • Based in: Manimajra, Chandigarh
  • Directors: Rohan and Pardeep Kumar Singh
  • Model: PCD pharma franchise and third-party manufacturer
  • Segments: analgesics, antibiotics and anti-infectives, anticold and anti-allergics, antipsychotics
  • Forms: tablets, capsules, softgelatin, syrups, injectables, ointments, beta-lactams, dry syrups, lotions, sachets and a dental range

How to choose and verify a Chandigarh pharma supplier

A franchise or third-party deal is only as strong as the licences behind it. Before signing, ask for the company's drug licence and GST registration, the manufacturing site's licence and WHO-GMP certificate, and a product list that prints the exact manufacturing address. Check the company name and incorporation details against the MCA record: several profiles in this guide show registry dates that differ from marketing claims, and the registry version is the one that matters in a dispute.

  • Match the entity: the name on the agreement, the invoice and the product labels should be the same legal entity.
  • Visit the plant, not just the office. Most offices here are small; the factory is usually in Baddi, Nalagarh, Derabassi or Barwala.
  • Confirm monopoly terms in writing: district boundaries, target conditions and what happens if targets are missed.
  • Check who actually manufactures. Several companies in this list use third-party plants, which is normal, but the plant's licence should be shared openly.
  • Start small. Place a trial order and check labelling, packaging and delivery times before committing to a full district deposit.

Frequently asked questions

Why are so many pharma companies registered in Chandigarh but manufacturing in Baddi?

Chandigarh offers offices, connectivity and a commercial address, while the Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh belt in Himachal Pradesh offers industrial land and the legacy of the 2003 central industrial package. Companies keep sales, franchise management and paperwork in the tricity and production in the belt, which is under an hour away by road.

What is a PCD pharma franchise?

PCD stands for propaganda-cum-distribution. A company gives a local partner the right to market its brands in a defined territory, often a single district, usually with monopoly rights. The partner promotes the products to doctors and chemists and handles local distribution, while the company supplies stock and promotional material.

How can I verify a company in this list?

Start with the MCA registry for the incorporation date, directors and registered office. Then ask the company for its drug licence and the manufacturing site's WHO-GMP certificate, and cross-check the address printed on product labels against the address the company gives you. Where this guide marks a figure as a company claim, it means the number comes from the company's own material.

Which is the oldest pharma company in this list?

By incorporation date, Ultra Chiron Pharmaceuticals, registered on 20 July 1993 at Industrial Area Phase II, Chandigarh. Logos Pharma dates its first manufacturing facility to 1994, according to its company profile, and Focus Healthcare follows with a 1998 founding.

Are PharmaAdda and Pharmahopers.com manufacturers?

No. Both are online platforms based in the tricity. PharmaAdda publishes directory lists of pharma companies, and PharmaHopers is a business-to-business marketplace where manufacturers, traders and distributors publish profiles and catalogues. They are useful for finding suppliers, but they do not make medicines themselves.

Does Sun Pharma really have a plant near Chandigarh?

Yes. Sun Pharmaceutical Industries operates its SEZ Unit-I formulation plant at Plot A-41, Industrial Area Phase VIII-A, SAS Nagar, Mohali. The plant came to Sun Pharma through the 2015 Ranbaxy acquisition, and the US FDA lifted its import alert in 2017.

content.rendered:
Ambala, in northern Haryana, hosts one of North India's densest clusters of pharmaceutical marketing companies. Most of them do not run large factories of their own. Instead, they build brands, appoint franchise partners across India, and have products made in certified plants in Haryana and Himachal Pradesh.

This guide profiles 86 pharma companies linked to Ambala, researched afresh from company websites, MCA-derived registries and trade directories. It covers PCD franchise firms, third-party manufacturers and specialists in ayurvedic, veterinary, nutraceutical and ophthalmic ranges, with the key facts a partner, supplier or job-seeker needs first.

Quick answer: the leading pharma companies in Ambala

If you need a shortlist fast, these are the Ambala names that stand out on track record, scale or specialism:

  • Casca Remedies — in business since 1988, with its own formulation plant and a portfolio of more than 1,400 products.
  • Ben Pharmaceuticals — also established in 1988; manufacturer, supplier and exporter with an unusually wide human and veterinary range.
  • Radicals Pharma — incorporated in 1986 and still manufacturing on the Ambala–Delhi highway.
  • Therawin Formulations — a 2003 partnership running PCD, generic, veterinary and contract-manufacturing divisions.
  • Orange Biotech — manufacturing since 2003, with neuro-psychiatry, gynae, paediatric and cardiac divisions.
  • Remedial Healthcare — PCD franchise specialist offering more than 300 products with monopoly rights.
  • Maksun Biotech — Saha-based franchisor with specialist divisions from gynae care to ophthalmics.
  • Vaxova Drugs — runs two manufacturing facilities and a range of more than 800 products.
  • Alvid Biocare — covers pharma, ayurvedic and veterinary lines, with 200+ products since 2012.
  • SBM Pharmaceuticals — marketing and third-party manufacturing since 2008, with herbal, cosmetics and IV divisions.
  • Granmed Pharma — franchise company working across eight therapy areas, from anti-infectives to CNS.
  • Zylig Lifesciences — manufacturer strong in critical-care injectables and general ranges.

Pharma in Ambala: how the cluster works

Ambala's pharma trade is concentrated in two adjoining urban areas, Ambala Cantt and Ambala City, with a further industrial pocket at Saha. The single most common business model is the PCD franchise, short for propaganda-cum-distribution, under which a company licenses its brands to a local partner for an agreed territory.

That model explains the geography. Dozens of companies share the same few streets around Nanhera Road and Kuldeep Nagar in Ambala Cantt, close to warehouses, transporters and the Ambala–Delhi highway (NH-44). Chandigarh and Panchkula are under an hour away, which keeps the cluster plugged into North India's biggest pharma trading hub.

Manufacturing often happens elsewhere. Many Ambala firms have their products made in WHO-GMP certified units in Himachal Pradesh towns such as Baddi, Kala Amb and Solan, where excise-free zones historically lowered costs, while some, such as Casca Remedies and Bovicure Pharma, run their own plants in or near Ambala.

What defines the Ambala cluster:

  • PCD first: most companies here are marketing and franchise businesses; partners typically receive monopoly rights for a district or pin-code area.
  • Two hubs: Ambala Cantt (Nanhera Road, Kuldeep Nagar) for franchise offices and godowns; the HSIIDC industrial estate at Saha for manufacturing units.
  • Certified supply: products are commonly made in WHO-GMP and ISO certified plants, frequently in Himachal Pradesh.
  • Specialists thrive: ayurvedic houses (Human Pharmacia, Shelmak), veterinary firms (Bovicure, Zenley) and ophthalmic specialists (Vaqure) sit alongside the generalists.
  • Beyond medicines: Ambala is also long established as a scientific and surgical instruments centre, often nicknamed Science City.

Quick comparison: 86 Ambala pharma companies at a glance

Detailed profiles: the 86 companies

1. Aconwell Pharma Pvt. Ltd.

Aconwell Pharma is a PCD pharma franchise company based in Ambala Cantt, with its office on Nanhera Road in the Kuldeep Nagar and Arjun Nagar area. It markets an allopathic range covering tablets, capsules, syrups, injectables, ointments and nutraceuticals, supplied to franchise partners across India.

How to choose an Ambala pharma company

Ambala gives a franchise partner or bulk buyer unusual choice in a small area, but the companies differ sharply in what sits behind the brand. Work through these points before comparing price lists:

  • Match the model to your plan: pick a PCD franchisor for territory marketing rights, a third-party manufacturer for your own label, or a firm such as Casca Remedies or Bovicure Pharma that manufactures in-house.
  • Match the range to your market: generalists cover the everyday prescriptions; specialists such as Vaqure (ophthalmic), Zenley (veterinary) or Human Pharmacia (ayurvedic) fit a focused practice or trade channel better.
  • Check who actually makes the product: many Ambala brands are made by partner plants in Himachal Pradesh. That is normal in this cluster, but the plant, not the brand office, is what to verify.
  • Get the monopoly terms in writing: territory definitions vary from a single pin code to a whole district, and they decide how much competition you face from the same brand.
  • Ask about partner support: visual aids, product literature, samples and training are standard offers in this market; confirm exactly what is included before you commit stock money.
  • Start with a trial order: a small first order tests dispatch speed, packaging quality and paperwork before you scale up.

What to verify before you sign or pay

None of this takes long, and every serious company in Ambala will expect the questions:

  • Company registration: for private limited firms, check the CIN and active status in MCA-derived registries; several profiles above list CINs to start from.
  • Your own licences: franchise partners are normally asked for a wholesale drug licence and GST registration before an agreement is issued; companies such as Bioversal Remedies and Vaxova Drugs state this upfront.
  • Manufacturing credentials: ask for the WHO-GMP certificate of the actual plant making your products, and check it names that plant and is in date.
  • Product approvals: ask for the approval or DCGI documentation for the specific formulations you plan to sell, not just a general company brochure.
  • Quality paperwork: confirm you will receive batch certificates of analysis with each consignment, and ask how expiry and damage claims are handled.
  • Agreement terms: read the franchise or manufacturing agreement for territory, payment terms, minimum orders and exit clauses before paying any advance.

Frequently asked questions

How many pharma companies are there in Ambala?

This guide profiles 86 companies with an Ambala base or a direct Ambala presence, and the true number trading in the district is higher once small traders are counted. The bulk of them sit in Ambala Cantt and Ambala City, with a manufacturing pocket at Saha.

What is a PCD pharma franchise?

PCD stands for propaganda-cum-distribution. A pharma company licenses its brands to a local partner, who markets and distributes them to doctors, chemists and hospitals in an agreed territory. Ambala companies commonly grant monopoly rights for that territory, which is why the model dominates this cluster.

What do I need to start a pharma franchise with an Ambala company?

Companies on this list typically ask for a wholesale drug licence and GST registration before issuing a franchise agreement. You will also need working capital for opening stock; the amount varies with the range and territory you choose, so confirm it in the written agreement.

Do Ambala pharma companies offer third-party manufacturing?

Yes. A large share of the companies profiled here, including Casca Remedies, Alvid Biocare, Biostem Pharma and Maksun Biotech, manufacture products for other brands. Production often takes place in WHO-GMP certified units, many of them in Himachal Pradesh's industrial areas.

Which parts of Ambala have the most pharma companies?

Nanhera Road and Kuldeep Nagar in Ambala Cantt hold the densest cluster of franchise offices and godowns. The HSIIDC industrial estate at Saha hosts manufacturing units, and Ambala City neighbourhoods such as Sena Nagar, Dhulkot, Model Town and Baldev Nagar hold many more firms.

Are there ayurvedic and veterinary specialists in Ambala?

Yes. Human Pharmacia, Shelmak Lifesciences and Mediwin Research and Healthcare specialise in ayurvedic products, while Bovicure Pharma and Zenley Animal Health focus on veterinary medicines and feed supplements. Several general firms also run ayurvedic or veterinary divisions alongside their main ranges.
