Quick highlights:

  • Latin dance is the specialisation: salsa, bachata and kizomba all have dedicated classes
  • Separate kids dance programme on the academy website
  • Wedding choreography and private classes offered alongside group batches
  • Zumba fitness classes, including a Zumba-at-home option

Rock 'N' Roll is the Latin-dance address in this guide. Its own website organises the academy around salsa, bachata and kizomba, with Bollywood, hip-hop and contemporary classes, Zumba fitness batches, a dedicated kids programme, wedding choreography and private lessons, all run from SCO 288 in Sector 35-D. The site names Ajay Bali as the face of the academy's salsa and bachata teaching.

The academy's own channel also lists dance classes at home among its options, which matters in Chandigarh, where a Sector 35 commute is easy for some and a deterrent for others. Local guides describe it as one of the city's longer-running western dance institutes; for couples dances and social Latin styles in particular, it is the most specialised option on this list.

VisitBest recommendation: Pick Rock ’N’ Roll for salsa, bachata or kizomba, for kids’ classes in Sector 35, or for wedding choreography with a Latin or Bollywood flavour.

Why students shortlist them:

  • The clearest Latin-dance specialisation in Chandigarh
  • Kids, adults, private and at-home formats all listed
  • Wedding choreography is a stated service

4. Jaskshan’s Dance Dacha

Locality: SCO 143-144, Sector 9-C, Madhya Marg | Styles: Latin American, Bhangra, Bharatnatyam, belly dance and Zumba | Classes: Kids to seniors

Quick highlights:

  • Founded by Jasmeet K. Shan, a state gold champion in Latin American dancesport, per the academy
  • Programmes for beginners through advanced levels, plus housewives, senior citizens and special kids, per its website
  • Licensed Zumba fitness sessions, per the academy
  • Unusual breadth: gymnastics for kids, a seniors programme and dance for special-needs children

Dance Dacha takes a different brief from the competition studios: dance as a daily lifestyle rather than a stage skill. Founder Jasmeet K. Shan, whom the academy profiles as a state gold champion in Latin American dancesport, has built the Sector 9-C studio around programmes for every age and stage: kids dance and gymnastics, a mom's fitness programme, licensed Zumba and dance-fitness batches, and special programmes for senior citizens and special-needs children.

The specialisation menu still covers the classic ground, with Latin American, Bhangra, Bharatnatyam, hip hop and Egyptian belly dance, plus wedding choreography and corporate workshops. If you are returning to movement after years away, or looking for a class where a parent and child can both belong, Dance Dacha is designed for exactly that.

VisitBest recommendation: Choose Dance Dacha for dance-led fitness, for seniors and mothers’ batches, or for inclusive programmes for special-needs children.

Why students shortlist them:

  • Founder is a Latin American dancesport champion, per the academy
  • Age range is the widest on this list, from kids to seniors
  • Zumba and dance fitness sit alongside classical and folk forms

5. Chandigarh Dance Academy

Locality: Stepping Stones School Campus, Sector 38-A | Styles: Kathak, semi-classical, folk, jazz and salsa | Run by: Prakriti Kunwar (per local profiles)

Quick highlights:

  • Based inside the Stepping Stones School campus in Sector 38-A
  • Run by Kathak dancer Prakriti Kunwar, trained under Shivji Mishra, per Chandigarh Bytes
  • One of the few academies pairing gharana-based Kathak with jazz and salsa
  • School-campus setting suits structured learning for children

Chandigarh Dance Academy works out of the Stepping Stones School campus in Sector 38-A, and its teaching reflects that setting: structured, technique-first and strong on Indian forms. Local profiles describe the academy as run by Prakriti Kunwar, a Kathak dancer trained under Shivji Mishra, and its style list pairs Kathak, taught with Jaipur and Lucknow gharana techniques, with semi-classical, folk, jazz funk and Latin salsa.

For parents, the combination is attractive: a child can build a genuine classical foundation, posture and rhythm discipline in Kathak while still sampling the western and stage styles most school functions demand. Ask about age-wise batches and annual performance opportunities when you visit the campus.

VisitBest recommendation: Shortlist Chandigarh Dance Academy for school-age children who should get real Kathak grounding without giving up stage styles.

Why students shortlist them:

  • Kathak is taught by gharana, not as a generic classical class
  • School-campus base in Sector 38-A
  • Classical and western styles under one roof

6. The ShowStoppers Dance Academy

Locality: SCO 42, Sector 37-D | Styles: Locking-popping, krumping, hip-hop, Bollywood and salsa | Focus: Street dance

Quick highlights:

  • Street styles are the core: locking-popping, krumping and freestyle hip-hop
  • Bollywood and Bhangra round out the stage repertoire
  • Teaching approach breaks routines into counts, per local guides
  • Sector 37-D base, near the Sector 38 school belt

The ShowStoppers Dance Academy in Sector 37-D is the street-dance specialist of this list. Local academy guides credit it with locking-popping, krumping and freestyle hip-hop at the core, plus Bollywood, Bhangra and salsa, and describe a teaching style that breaks complex routines into manageable counts so beginners can reach choreography that looks advanced.

That makes it a natural pick for teenagers and young adults whose goal is the stage: college fests, competitions and battles rather than fitness. If your interest is specifically in popping, locking or krump, this is the Chandigarh academy whose published style list is built around them.

VisitBest recommendation: Choose ShowStoppers if street styles, not fitness or classical forms, are what you want to learn.

Why students shortlist them:

  • Beginner-friendly breakdown of routines, per local guides

Freedom2Dance, on the top floor of SCO 291 in Sector 32-D, is a dance-and-fitness studio in the full sense: its directory listings run from classical, hip-hop, contemporary, jazz funk and Bollywood to salsa, ballroom, Zumba and dance fitness. The studio teaches kids, teens and adults, in private and group formats from beginner to advanced levels, and lists online classes for those who cannot reach Sector 32 regularly. VisitBest recommendation: Shortlist Freedom2Dance for ballroom and Latin social dancing, or for a single studio covering both dance styles and fitness.

Also Worth Knowing About Dance Classes in Chandigarh

The map follows the sectors. Academies cluster where their students live: Madhya Marg and Sectors 8 and 9 in the north, Sectors 17, 21 and 22 in the centre, the 30s belt for technique and classical schools, and Sectors 44 to 47 for the southern neighbourhoods. There is almost certainly a listed academy within a short drive of your home sector, which matters more for consistency than a famous name across town.

Three academies teach inside schools. Chandigarh Dance Academy works from Stepping Stones School in Sector 38-A, Rockstar Academy from the AKSIPS campus in Sector 45-A and Gurdeep Singh Academy from Rainbow International School. Campus academies suit children: familiar premises, school-year calendars and annual-function stages built in.

The classical and western worlds rarely overlap. Only Pracheen Kala Kendra and Chandigarh Dance Academy build their identity on Indian classical forms, and only the Kendra examines and certifies them. Everything else on this list is a studio model: join a batch, learn choreography, perform when the studio performs.

The Tricity is bigger than this list. This guide covers Chandigarh city itself. Mohali has its own established studios, Step2Step being the best known, and dancers near the borders often compare both cities before joining. FAQs About Dance Academies in Chandigarh

Which is the best dance academy in Chandigarh for classical dance?

Pracheen Kala Kendra in Sector 35-B is the clear answer for classical dance with credentials: founded in 1956, it runs graded certificate and diploma courses in Kathak, Bharatnatyam, Odissi, Manipuri and Kuchipudi and conducts its own examinations. For Kathak taught within a school-campus setting, Chandigarh Dance Academy in Sector 38-A, run by a Kathak dancer per local profiles, is the other specialist on this list.

What dance styles can I learn in Chandigarh?

Almost everything mainstream. The academies in this guide between them teach Kathak, Bharatnatyam, Odissi, Manipuri and Kuchipudi; hip-hop, locking-popping, krumping and breaking; Bollywood and Bhangra; salsa, bachata, kizomba, ballroom and other Latin forms; contemporary, jazz and ballet; belly dance; and Zumba and dance fitness. Rare styles worth noting: kizomba and ballroom at Urban School of Dance and Freedom2Dance, and Egyptian belly dance at Dance Dacha.

Are there dance classes for kids in Chandigarh?

Yes, at many levels. Rock 'N' Roll runs a dedicated kids programme in Sector 35-D, Dance Dacha runs kids dance and gymnastics in Sector 9-C, Rockstar Academy in Sector 45-A is built around children and school functions, and The Dance Mafia lists batches for under-10s. Campus-based academies inside schools, in Sectors 38-A and 45-A, are often the most convenient for school-age children.

Do Chandigarh dance academies offer wedding choreography?

Yes. Rock 'N' Roll lists wedding choreography among its services, DanceworkZ in Sector 18-D headlines wedding choreography and offers home tuition for rehearsals, Dance Dacha lists basic, theme-based and destination wedding choreography on its website, and Steps Growing Academy lists wedding choreography classes on JustDial. Book choreographers early in the wedding season, and agree the number of rehearsals and the final music edit in writing.

How much do dance classes in Chandigarh cost?

Fees vary by academy, style and batch type, and academies revise them by season, so this guide does not publish a fee table. As a rule, group batches cost less than private classes, certified multi-year courses price differently from monthly studio batches, and wedding choreography is quoted per performance or package. Ask each shortlisted academy for its current fee, the number of classes it covers each week, and its makeup-class policy before paying.

Conclusion

Chandigarh can take you from a first Kathak position at a 1956 institution to a salsa social in Sector 35, a krump battle in Sector 37 or a sangeet performance choreographed at your own home. Shortlist two or three academies whose stated style and sector match your goal, take a trial class at each, and judge the instructor and the batch rather than the brochure. The academy you will still be attending in six months is the right one, and in this city it is probably closer than you think.
